title: Onboarding sprint plan for LLM integration
body:
Purpose
This doc is a condensed sprint-style plan to onboard a mid-market customer for an LLM-powered feature (search+rerank + small-context summarization) as a 4-week POC. The goal is to validate latency/cost targets, validate data security controls for private deployment, and deliver a working integration that the customer can demo to their product owners.

Scope (what we will deliver)
- Hosted integration with a dedicated test namespace (or Private deployment if requested)
- End-to-end request path: client -> Redwood API -> chosen model variant -> application-level post-processing (rerank/summarize)
- Performance baseline (p50/p95 latency, cost per 1K tokens) and small load test (up to 20 concurrent users)
- Security checklist verified: data flow diagram, KMS integration validated, audit log sampling
- Workshop + handoff docs + runbook for the customer engineering team

Out of scope
- Production traffic cutover, scale >100 concurrent users, custom model training, full compliance certification (SOC2 audit)

Success criteria (POC acceptance)
- Functional: demo scenario reproduces within 2 steps of customer test script; correctness metrics (precision@10 for rerank >= baseline threshold)
- Performance: p95 generation latency <= 700ms for 512-token context in dedicated environment, cost <= target estimate (+/- 20%)
- Security: KMS integration established and basic audit logs appear in the console; no plaintext secrets in logs

High-level timeline (4 weeks)
Week 0 (pre-sprint, 3 working days)
- Kickoff workshop scheduled, invite list finalized (customer PM, SE, infra contact) — owner: Rohit
- Customer adjudicates access: test data subset, network access (IP allowlist / VPC peering) — owner: Customer infra
- Create repo skeleton + initial API keys (ephemeral) — owner: Jordan

Week 1 (environment + data prep)
- Host kickoff workshop (2 hours): objectives, integration pattern choices, security Q&A — owner: Rohit
- Provision test environment: dedicated namespace or private deployment staging — owner: Maya
- Data ingestion plumbing: customer provides sample dataset, format mapping, redaction checklist — owner: Priya
- Acceptance criteria: environment reachable, sample dataset loaded into staging

Week 2 (model integration + feature wiring)
- Implement inference calls and post-processing pipeline for rerank + summarization — owner: Jordan
- Instrument telemetry hooks for latency, token counts, errors — owner: Maya
- Small-scale validation runs and unit tests for edge cases (truncated contexts, null inputs) — owner: Priya
- Acceptance criteria: demo flow end-to-end with sample dataset; telemetry visible in console

Week 3 (load testing + quality evaluation)
- Run scripted load tests (10-20 concurrent simulated users), measure p50/p95 and token throughput — owner: Site Reliability (Liam)
- Evaluate output quality on curated prompts; run automated checks and manual review — owner: Priya
- Tune batching/quantization recommendations via Redwood Optimize suggestions — owner: Maya
- Acceptance criteria: performance targets met or tuning plan documented; quality gates passed for >80% prompt set

Week 4 (documentation, workshop, handoff)
- Run customer demo and walkthrough of runbook, rollout checklist — owner: Rohit
- Deliver artifact pack: config snippets, sample prompts, failover policy, escalation contacts — owner: Jordan
- Handoff meeting and follow-up ticket backlog for production readiness items — owner: Rohit
- Acceptance criteria: customer signs off on POC checklist and identifies production owner

Task tracker (high-level items)
- [ ] Kickoff workshop calendar + slide deck (owner: Rohit)
- [ ] Test environment provisioned + credentials rotated (owner: Maya)
- [ ] Data ingest script and basic redaction applied (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Integration PR merged; CI smoke tests pass (owner: Jordan)
- [ ] Telemetry dashboard created (owner: Maya)
- [ ] Load test run and report (owner: Liam)
- [ ] Final demo scheduled + acceptance form (owner: Rohit)

Risk map and mitigations
- Risk: Customer cannot provide representative data in time -> Mitigation: synthetic dataset recipe + minimal stub that reproduces edge cases; escalate on day 2
- Risk: Network/VPC keepalive restrictions block egress to hosted API -> Mitigation: plan for Private deployment sandbox (pre-approved image) and run local mock if needed
- Risk: Latency higher than target because of long context lengths -> Mitigation: recommend prefix caching, reduce context window, provide quantization/variant with lower memory footprint
- Risk: Secrets or PHI in logs -> Mitigation: enforce logging redaction, review CloudWatch/console retention settings during Week 1

Decisions to capture in sprint
- Model variant selection policy: start with mid-size open model (e.g., MPT-7B quantized) and benchmark; only escalate to larger models if quality targets require it
- Routing policy: prefer dedicated capacity for latency SLOs; fallback to hosted with higher latency if capacity constrained

Security & compliance quick checklist
- Ensure KMS key tied to customer project + sample encryption test -> done by Week 1
- Confirm audit log entries show request IDs and userIDs (no raw prompts logged) -> Week 2
- Data retention setting reviewed with customer (30/90/365) -> documented in runbook

Kickoff workshop agenda (90–120 minutes)
- 0:00–0:10 Introductions and objectives (Rohit)
- 0:10–0:25 Customer product walkthrough / success metrics (Customer PM)
- 0:25–0:40 Integration architecture options (hosted vs. private) (Maya)
- 0:40–0:55 Data handling, redaction strategy, and audit requirements (Priya)
- 0:55–1:10 Telemetry and SLO targets; demo acceptance criteria (Liam)
- 1:10–1:30 Q&A and immediate actions (all)

Meeting notes template (use during workshop)
- Attendees:
- Decisions made:
- Open action items and owners:
- Blockers:

Handoff & follow-up deliverables
- Post-demo runbook (1 pager) with failover and escalation steps
- PR checklist for production (security review, performance benchmarks, SLOs)
- List of post-POC tickets and estimated effort

Appendix: quick commands and snippets (placeholders)
- API call example: curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <EPHEMERAL_KEY>' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"mpt-7b-q8","input":"..."}'
- Minimal telemetry query: filter by request_id, aggregate p95 token latency
- Redaction notes: sample regex patterns and redaction script link (linked artifact)

Notes & open questions (to capture during kickoff)
- Will customer require on-prem packaging or is VPC sufficient?
- Are there existing SSO/KMS constraints that will add slippage?
- Which internal stakeholder signs off on cost estimates?

Document history
- 2025-11-04 created by Rohit Patel (initial draft)
- 2026-01-12 internal review comments added (Maya)
- 2026-02-20 updated with load test owner and acceptance criteria (Liam)
